Theme

Computing & programming · Work & responsibility

scan verb

a document, into a computer

also scanner, scanning, scan a document

* our formation

Cic. Verr. 2.2.189: litterae … dē tabulīs in librōs trānsferuntur (Lewis & Short)

* (our own formation) trānsferō, trānsferre, trānstulī, trānslātum

verb, irregular; in full, in computātrum trānsferre, conjugation

carry over: scan

Our choice: no reference work has a verb for scanning. Classically trānsferre is to carry something over, and also to copy writing from one book into another (Lewis & Short); scanning carries the page over into the computer.

Other words

  • scānsōrium, scānsōriī n. — a scanner

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 262; Andresian p. 14

    Built on scandere, which classically means to climb, or to scan verse; the English sense of scan does not come through in Latin.

Examples

  • Chartam in computātrum trānsfer.

    Scan the page into the computer.composed

See also photocopy, computer, document.

SourcesLewis & Short: transfero · Lewis & Short: scando

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 262.

Anna Andresian, Vocabula Picta (2014), p. 14.
